lead.headline: Nvidia's board investigates CEO Jensen Huang after reports a suspected Chinese intelligence asset targeted him
signal: Nvidia's key customers and export-control politics are now tied to its CEO's conduct. If the probe finds leaks, the risk falls on China chip sales and on Huang's access to Trump.
lead.hook: Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation after reports that Jensen Huang was ==the target of a foreign intelligence effort==, and Huang admitted an affair with the woman at its centre.
points: Alice Huang (no relation) is an executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed. US officials concluded she was passing information to Beijing, the New York Times reported. The Chinese Embassy denies any spying.
Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips over two years, making it one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.
Independent directors with outside counsel will run the probe. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. Huang, 63, stays CEO.
Republican lawmakers want a closed-door briefing from Huang next week. A separate call asks him to appear before Congress on November 18.
Trump downplayed the matter and said he would take Huang on his Asia trip. Nvidia fell 3.1%, the heaviest drag on the S&P 500, in a week when Nasdaq lost nearly $1 trillion.
lead.editors_read: The board's finding matters less for its legal outcome than for whether Congress uses the episode to tighten chip export rules. Warren is pushing bipartisan legislation. Huang's closeness to Trump protects him in the White House but not with Congress. Markets will price any hint that Megaspeed-type buyers face new scrutiny.

frontpage.headline: Anthropic buys $3.4 billion of gas generators to power its data centres, FT reports
signal: Power, not chips, is becoming the scarce input. Peers have done similar deals: xAI bought turbines for $2 billion and Alphabet bought energy developer Intersect.
If a junk rating holds, Anthropic's borrowing cost for this build-out rises.
frontpage.hook: Anthropic agreed to pay ==$3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators==, the largest known single purchase of power equipment by an AI lab, the FT reports.
points: The supplier is San Antonio-based OnePWR Solutions, and the deal was struck in late September. It includes the engineering and construction needed to install the equipment.
OnePWR ordered the Caterpillar generators about two years ago but needed financing. Anthropic planned to buy power from it, then took over the orders instead.
Anthropic did not buy OnePWR, and no staff moved over. Equipment lead times stretch years, so AI firms are going around traditional suppliers.
Anthropic has disclosed nearly $900 billion of computing commitments through 2045. Its monthly payments to lease SpaceX computing are expected to reach $3.1 billion by year-end.
Blackstone has warned investors that Anthropic might get a junk credit rating rather than the investment-grade rating expected.
frontpage.editors_read: Taking over a queue of existing equipment orders buys years of lead time that cash alone cannot. It also adds fixed costs and debt ahead of an IPO. Investors will weigh that against the credit warning.

frontpage.headline: India's white-collar hiring up 14%, but software engineering hiring up only 1%
signal: The headline averages two markets. Specialist AI, data and engineering roles are growing; generic software delivery is flat.
November's index, due in early December, is the first without a festive distortion.
frontpage.hook: Naukri's JobSpeak index rose ==14% year on year in October==, but software engineering and QA hiring rose just 1%.
points: The index stood at 2,836 against 2,480 in October 2025. Naukri says Diwali fell in October 2025, depressing last year's base. It also fell from 3,053 in September.
Production and manufacturing roles rose 39%, automobiles 36% (auto R&D 53%), AI and machine learning 32%, and global capability centres 18%.
IT and software services industry hiring rose 5%. An ICRIER survey of 651 IT firms found close to two-thirds classing developers as significantly exposed to AI.
Experienced hires are in demand: professionals with 13 to 16 years and those with 16+ each rose 22%. Fresher hiring rose 15%. Hyderabad led metros at 15%.

frontpage.headline: Foreign investors put ₹46,000 crore into Indian stocks in five sessions as the AI trade cracks
signal: India's low AI exposure, a weakness all year, is now an advantage. If Brent stays below $100 and US inflation is not hot, the inflows have room to continue.
frontpage.hook: Foreign portfolio investors bought ==₹45,970 crore of Indian equities in five sessions==, ending two months of net selling and lifting the Nifty 50 by 8.6%.
points: The Nifty's week was its strongest since February 2021. The index is down 4.21% for the year, having been nearly 15% below its start-of-year level at its low.
The rupee rose 0.6% to 93.91 per dollar, its strongest since April, from about 95.4 a week earlier.
Brent crude fell about 13% to roughly $98 on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation after the midterms. Cheaper oil helps India's inflation, current account and rupee.
Funds are rotating out of AI-linked names. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday, Korea and Japan fell about 6% on Friday, and Indian IT stocks rose.
US CPI (inflation data) is due Tuesday, November 10. With a December US rate hike nearly priced in, a hot reading could push the dollar and yields up.

frontpage.headline: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 crore subsidy for 92 GWh of grid storage by 2030-31
signal: Non-fossil capacity is 300.5 GW but solar output is zero at the evening peak. If storage gets built on time, coal's balancing role shrinks.
Execution risk: pumped hydro needs clearances and long construction, and the 40% domestic content rule must be met while cell capacity is still being built.
frontpage.hook: India's Cabinet approved a ==₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme== (a subsidy that covers the shortfall in a project's returns) to build 92 GWh of grid storage by 2030-31.
points: Total investment is expected at ₹97,600 crore, close to seven rupees per rupee of public support. The new capacity equals 170% of India's present grid-scale storage base.
The split is 60 GWh pumped hydro, 30 GWh batteries and 2 GWh for emerging technologies. Distribution companies are eligible and capacity is allocated by competitive bidding.
Batteries must meet a 40% domestic content requirement, creating demand for Indian cells. The existing PLI scheme for cell manufacturing targets 50 GWh, of which 10 GWh is for grid use.
Storage bid tariffs fell from about ₹10.18 per kWh in 2022-23 to about ₹2.1 per kWh by December 2025, without subsidy, assuming two cycles a day.
The Central Electricity Authority estimates India needs about 411 GWh by 2031-32, so 92 GWh covers under a quarter of that.

frontpage.headline: Zipline raises $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation for drone delivery
signal: If FAA rules and local approvals slow, the Walmart and Uber targets slip. The valuation assumes they do not.
frontpage.hook: Zipline raised ==$1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation==, nearly triple the $7.6 billion it was valued at in January.
points: Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led. Uber, Fidelity, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan and others took part. Funds go to US manufacturing, hiring and a national network.
Walmart and Zipline plan 300 additional sites under a multi-year deal. Uber targets one million Zipline deliveries a day by 2029.
The CEO says flying beyond visual line of sight was illegal in the US for the company's first 10 years, so it launched abroad. The FAA's proposed Part 108 rule would make it routine.
Zipline says its drones have flown 150 million autonomous commercial miles with zero safety incidents. Amazon __plans to grow its drone service from 11__ to about 500 US locations by year-end.
Mordor Intelligence forecasts the delivery drone market at $4.40 billion by 2030, so the valuation is nearly five times that.

frontpage.headline: Hyperscalers favour southern wind-solar hybrids over Kutch and Rajasthan, CleanMax says
signal: Transmission access and curtailment risk are now pricing power for developers. Project location matters as much as tariff.
frontpage.hook: Tech giants buying renewable power in India are choosing ==wind-solar hybrids in the south== over Kutch and Rajasthan because they fear curtailment, CleanMax management said.
points: Curtailment means the grid forces a plant to cut output. CleanMax's Bikaner plant saw about 70% in the first quarter, nearly 50% in July-August, 44% after, and 26% in October. It cost about 5% of first-half EBITDA.
Hyperscalers want projects connected to the central transmission utility network, and prefer hybrids because a combined profile matches demand better.
All of CleanMax's CTU-connected capacity through September 2028 is sold. It reserves CTU capacity for hyperscalers over smelters and has applied for 2 GW more.
Hyperscalers are 27-28% of its 6.2 GW contracted capacity, and it holds about 35% of hyperscaler volumes contracted in India. No wind-solar-storage data centre deal is signed yet.

stories.headline: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer and fold its code storage into Codex
signal: OpenAI is buying a component it already depends on, which strengthens Codex's position against other coding assistants.
stories.hook: OpenAI announced on November 4 that it will acquire developer-tool startup Pierre Computer, whose Code Storage tool will be integrated into Codex.
points: Pierre's file navigation and code review libraries already power parts of Codex, per Technobezz.
Code Storage is a distributed storage system for code, with Git storage, review and navigation tools. Price and closing date are not stated in the snippets.
OpenAI says Pierre's open-source projects stay freely available, and Code Storage customers can keep using it after closing.

also.line: RBA Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said AI-related investment will add to demand and near-term price pressure while the central bank is aggressively raising rates to fight inflation.
Meta is reportedly preparing to launch its Muse AI assistant in the UK, per The Times. Muse adoption is a focus of Meta's third-quarter earnings.
CSE report: hailstorms hit 27 states on 80% of days in April-May 2026; 0.73 million hectares of crops were affected in the pre-monsoon season, second-highest after 2023.

stories.headline: Fewer Bay of Bengal monsoon depressions are shifting India's rain south
signal: Farms and water planners in eastern and central India face less dependable monsoon rain, if the trend continues.
stories.hook: Monsoon depressions over the Bay of Bengal ==fell from 26 in the 1980s to 10 in 2010-2020==, moving rainfall away from eastern and central India.
points: Monsoon depressions are low-pressure systems that bring days of widespread rain. The sharpest drop was in August, when they normally peak.

The equatorial Indian Ocean and western Pacific have warmed more than the northern Bay of Bengal. That weakens Walker and Hadley circulations (global air-flow systems), so fewer winds converge over the bay.
Rainfall fell along the usual paths, including central India and the Gangetic plains, while parts of the southern peninsula got more.
The study of 1980-2020 data comes from IITM Pune, JNU and Central University of Haryana. Researchers say agriculture, groundwater recharge and water supply could be affected.

stories.headline: New-age tech firms post profits in Q2 FY27 despite a muted festive start
signal: Analyst Atul Thakkar expects earnings delivery, not growth stories, to drive returns over the next 12-18 months. Falling volume-to-revenue ratios at logistics firms are the risk to that.
stories.hook: Nine of 11 large new-age tech stocks reported a net profit in Q2 FY27, with combined profit up about ₹1,100-1,400 crore year on year.
points: EBITDA grew faster than revenue at all nine profitable firms, a sign of operating leverage (costs rising slower than sales). Swiggy and Meesho still report losses.
Logistics: Shadowfax revenue rose 57%. Delhivery express shipments grew 32% against 22% revenue growth. Shiprocket posted a ₹60 lakh profit versus a ₹20.3 crore loss.

Fintech: all major firms were profitable. The proposed UPI merchant discount rate (a fee on merchant transactions) is postponed beyond the festive period; insurance commission changes could hit PB Fintech.
E-commerce: Nykaa's profit more than tripled. Honasa's profit rose 87% to ₹73.2 crore on 36% revenue growth to ₹731.2 crore.
Online festive sales slipped from last year and conversion on premium products fell.

stories.headline: Pronto's house-help cameras feed a new physical AI venture in San Francisco
signal: If synthetic data improves, demand for human-captured footage could shrink. Value could accrue to foreign model owners rather than Indian workers.
stories.hook: Pronto's home-services workers wear cameras whose footage trains AI, and founder Anjali Sardana has set up ==Provision Labs, a physical AI venture, to collect that data==.
points: Pronto says it has served over half a million households in 11 cities. Its opt-in Verified service, launched in July, has workers wear cameras. Provision Labs, founded in October, is acquiring Mumbai-based Basilisk Industries.
The company says raw footage is deleted, and an anonymised copy is kept for AI training after 48 hours. Pronto declined to say how it and Provision Labs work together.
Robots need real-world interaction data. Goldman Sachs estimates general-purpose robots may need around 10 million hours.
Pronto says over half of Verified workers earn above ₹40,000 a month; Human Archive cites $1-10 per hour. Data collection rates fell 30% between January and June.
An openDemocracy investigation found workers at two Delhi factories wore cameras without being told why. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act is scheduled for implementation in May 2027.

also.line: Sequoia closed its London office, merged its early-stage and growth teams and ended its Scouts programme; the FT frames this as undoing former leader Roelof Botha's legacy.

stories.headline: Solar Industries Q2 revenue jumps 69% to ₹3,519 crore on defence growth
signal: Revenue is shifting toward defence. If the order book converts, defence becomes the main earnings driver.
stories.hook: Solar Industries' Q2 FY27 revenue rose ==69% to ₹3,519 crore== and profit after tax rose to ₹650 crore from ₹361 crore.
points: EBITDA was ₹1,021 crore against ₹582 crore, a 29.02% margin. H1 revenue was ₹7,187 crore, up 70%.
Defence revenue was ₹1,002 crore, 29% of the customer basket against 24% a year earlier. The order book is ₹20,178 crore, of which defence is ₹17,568 crore.
Domestic explosives fell to 27% of the basket from 29%, and international to 43% from 46%.
Management __expects to surpass FY27 revenue guidance of ₹14,000 crore__ and annual margin guidance of around 28%.

stories.headline: French startup Alta Ares wins 16 lots in NATO's counter-drone framework
signal: Preselected catalogues shorten procurement for allies, favouring suppliers with battlefield data.
stories.hook: Alta Ares won ==16 lots in NATO's counter-drone framework==, the most among five suppliers, letting allies buy directly without new tenders.
points: The other suppliers are Northrop Grumman, Axon, Quantum Systems and OSL. The framework is a preselected catalogue under NATO's Rapid Adoption Action Plan; allies can buy or lease.
The company says it is the only supplier selected for area defence across static, transportable and on-the-move categories, covering sites such as air bases and munition depots.
Its software uses data from Ukraine since 2024. The X-Lock interceptor has a stated range of over 15 km and speed of 310 km/h; the Black Bird roughly doubles both.
It has not said which configurations are in the framework, and is boosting production with partners.

stories.headline: Gujarat startups raise ₹287 crore across six ventures, mostly in hardware-heavy deep tech
signal: Hardware startups need years of testing before revenue. The ₹287 crore total reflects capital announced, not adoption.
stories.hook: Six Gujarat startups raised ==over ₹287 crore in four months==, with five of the six building specialised technology rather than pure software.
points: Insurtech In __Risk Labs raised $27 million__ (about ₹255.8 crore) in a Series A co-led by Bessemer and Northpoint. The total is skewed by this one round.
Cellegant raised ₹2.6 crore for hydrogen fuel-cell drivetrains for drones and plans to move its 35-kg drone from technology readiness level three to six in 6-12 months.

Spectra Gaze (space and defence imaging sensors) raised a ₹3.7 crore seed; Edgeverse (edge AI vehicle safety) got ₹3 crore from GVFL; Cosmochute (lunar mobility) raised $1.5 million; Bucketlistt.com raised ₹7.6 crore.
The report gives no deployment, revenue or crash-reduction data for these ventures.

also.line: UK announced £138 million for quantum sensing procurement, £35 million for quantum networking testbeds and £12 million for a commercialisation skills centre to speed adoption.

stories.headline: Collapse of Paraguay's digital bank ueno topples the president
signal: Analysts say the damage to Paraguay's investment reputation may outlast the resolution.
stories.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
stories.hook: Paraguay's digital bank ueno collapsed in five days, freezing the savings of nearly 3 million customers, and President Santiago Peña was ==impeached and arrested==.
points: Ueno, launched in 2021, drew roughly half the country's 6.5 million people. Public bodies, including the state pension fund, held about $850 million there as of June.
Leaked regulatory reports warned of excessive lending to certain companies. On Tuesday the central bank put ueno into resolution after it breached minimum solvency requirements.
Peña had been a business partner of ueno's owner group until March 2025 and named its former president, Carlos Carvallo, to head the central bank. Both are charged with breach of trust and others.
About $160 million has been paid to nearly 1.2 million savers under the deposit guarantee. Authorities say the crisis is confined to ueno. Vice president Pedro Alliana is now president.

stories.headline: Redington and Ingram Micro gain as India's AI data centre build-out lifts server sales
signal: Distributors earn thin margins but gain from deal size. If the build-out slows, their growth reverts to phones.
stories.hook: AI compute now makes up roughly a fifth of Redington's and Ingram Micro's revenue and is among their ==fastest-growing lines==, helped by India's data centre build-out.
points: Redington ended the quarter with ₹430 billion in revenue, up 23% sequentially. Its software and technology solutions businesses rose 71% and 45% in H1, against 41% overall growth.
Management says AI servers with GPUs have average selling prices often 4x higher. Large deals above ₹3,800 crore were about 9% of group revenue, many from data centres.
Phones and laptops are three-fifths of the two firms' business. Ingram Micro India was about $5 billion, a tenth of its 2025 revenue.
Motilal Oswal puts India's data centre capacity at about 1.3 GW, with 7.1 GW more announced over four years.

also.line: Gita Gopinath warns the roughly $1 trillion being invested in AI in 2026 alone may be hard to recover through profits, raising the risk of a market correction and a US recession.

stories.headline: Microsoft opens fourth India cloud region in Hyderabad
signal: The 20% versus 3% gap is Microsoft's own framing of the opportunity. Power and land will limit how fast capacity is added.
stories.hook: Microsoft launched its ==fourth India cloud region in Hyderabad==, joining Pune, Chennai and Mumbai, as part of a $20.5 billion India commitment.
points: Microsoft's India head says India generates nearly 20% of the world's data but holds only about 3% of global data centre capacity.
India has about 2 GW of data centre capacity. Microsoft expects 12-14 GW by 2035.
He says demand is strong and the constraint is infrastructure, as businesses and government move AI from experiments to deployment.

also.line: Delhi's PM2.5 hit 767 micrograms per cubic metre at Anand Vihar on Deepavali night, over 51 times the WHO 24-hour limit, as firecrackers were burst past the Supreme Court's 10 p.m. deadline.
also.source: India Latest News: Top National Headlines Today & Breaking News | The Hindu

stories.headline: Cop31 opens in Turkey with the US absent and a record El Niño
signal: Without the US, climate finance depends on other rich countries, so the finance fight likely drives the outcome.
stories.hook: Cop31 opens Monday in Antalya with nearly 190 countries, the US sending no delegation for the second year, and ==temperatures already above the 1.5C Paris limit==.
points: Australia presides over negotiations while Turkey hosts. Australia's Chris Bowen wants a tangible, implementation-focused outcome. Only 0.2% of climate finance goes to small island states for adaptation.
Friction is expected between rich and poor countries over who pays for climate impacts and the slow pace of emissions cuts.
Turkey wants a target of 35% of final energy from electricity by 2035, which faces opposition from some.
Twenty US Democratic members of Congress are attending. The Iran war has pushed many countries to see fossil fuels as expensive and vulnerable to shocks.

stories.headline: Trump says 'Iron Gate' blockade on Iran is in effect; drone strike cuts power in Iraq's Kurdistan
signal: Energy infrastructure in the region stays exposed while talks continue. Brent has fallen to about $98 on de-escalation hopes.
stories.source: Al Jazeera – Breaking News, World News and Video from Al Jazeera
stories.hook: A drone strike on Iraq's Khor Mor gas facility left ==more than 70% of Iraq's Kurdish region without power==.
points: The strike caused a fire at the Khor Mor gas facility in northern Iraq.
Trump says the latest US blockade of Iran's land supply routes, called 'Iron Gate', is in effect.
He says renewed strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress on Iran's nuclear programme and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: KPMG: 52% of Indian CEOs plan some workforce cuts, yet 92% expect headcount to grow
signal: Roles are being redefined rather than cut overall, with entry-level jobs most under review.
stories.hook: KPMG's survey finds ==52% of Indian CEOs plan workforce cuts in some areas==, up from 50% in 2025, while 92% expect total headcount to grow over three years.
points: The survey covered 125 Indian CEOs of firms with over $500 million revenue (1,400 globally). 78% of Indian CEOs call AI a top investment priority.
86% are reviewing skills needed for entry-level roles, versus 76% globally. 87% prioritise retaining and retraining high-potential staff, up from 70%.
62% __expect to put 11-20% of their budgets into AI__, and 70% expect returns in one to three years. 46% say agentic AI (software that executes tasks autonomously) already has a significant impact.
Ethical challenges are the top barrier at 64%; 53% cite inconsistent regional AI regulation, against 41% globally.

also.line: AI, data and cybersecurity skills were 30.3% of GCC tech hiring demand in July-September, up from 25.8% the previous quarter, even as total GCC tech hiring demand fell 3.5%, Quess says.

stories.headline: Cheap antipersonnel mines are back in Ukraine, driven by 3D printing, microcontrollers and drones
signal: Cheap, easily copied weapons leave civilian danger for decades after conflicts end, and demining capacity must catch up.
stories.hook: Antipersonnel mines are returning despite the 1997 Ottawa Treaty, enabled by ==3D printing, microcontrollers and drone delivery==.
points: 3D printing lets frontline units make their own mines in varied shapes and colours. Microcontrollers trigger mines using magnetic, motion, heat, vibration or Bluetooth sensors.
Drones place mines precisely on paths and around trenches. A UN commission and rights groups report Russian forces use drones to drop mines to target civilians in Kherson.
Ukraine suspended implementation of the treaty, and Poland, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia are pulling out.
An explosive-ordnance disposal consultant predicts these methods will spread worldwide, and says demining agencies must update their training.

opportunities.name: Top Business Schools Present: Application Tips (Virtual)
opportunities.summary: Admissions reps from ten MBA programmes, including Booth, Harvard, Stanford, Wharton, Kellogg, MIT Sloan and Columbia, share application tips. Online; the link is sent after registration.
